title: Cardinality-aware index rewrite and online compact migrations
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Background: The control plane has accumulated several overlapping indexes on high-cardinality columns (tenant_id, user_id, entity_type) and broad composite indexes left from early product iterations. These indexes bloat storage, slow write amplification, and cause unpredictable planner choices on multi-tenant query hot paths (route resolution, tenant metadata lookups, and audit log joins).

Scope: Replace blanket composite indexes with cardinality-aware, partial, and expression-based indexes, and migrate large tables with zero-downtime online DDL. This ticket covers planning, staging run, two production migrations, and capacity tuning post-migration. Non-goals: application-level query rewrites or multi-region topology changes (those are separate initiatives).

Goals:
- Reduce total secondary index size for affected tables by >45%
- Improve p95 read latency on control-plane hot endpoints by 20%
- Keep write amplification and DDL-related replication lag within safe thresholds during migrations

Strategy summary:
1) Audit: Use pg_stat_user_indexes, EXPLAIN ANALYZE samples, and recent slow query logs to identify redundant/unused indexes and high-cardinality columns.
2) Design: For each candidate table create a cardinality map and propose either (a) partial index (WHERE region IS NOT NULL), (b) expression index (lower(name)), or (c) covering index scoped to the most selective predicates.
3) Safety: Use pt-online-schema-change for MySQL-compatible clusters or pg_repack and CONCURRENTLY CREATE INDEX in Postgres. All online DDL must have an explicit capacity window and rollback SQL prepared.
4) Migration: Run staged builds in staging environment; then small shard-by-shard rollouts with traffic shaping and extended monitoring.
5) Observability: Add temporary metrics and traces for index usage and replication lag, add rollback hooks to the runbook.

Deliverables:
- Index proposal doc with per-table choices and size/benefit estimates
- Staging migration runbook and scripts
- Two production migrations (tenant_metadata, audit_events) with rollbacks
- Post-migration analysis and follow-up tidy tasks
